sentences.text: The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 31.5.2008 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ahmedabad Rural in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.406 of 21993, whereby the learned Tribunal granted compensation of Rs.4,72,000/- to the claimants with 8.5 % interest per annum from the date of filing the claim petition till realization.

2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
2.1
On 21-9-92 the accident took place.
The original claimant was going on Scooter No.G.U.S.2545.
At that time, Fiat Car No.G.U.K. 9000 came in full speed and in rash & negligent manner, and dashed with the scooter, in which,he had sustained fractures and the injuries on other parts of body.

3. Learned advocate for the appellant found fault with the judgment and award passed by the learned Tribunal on the issue of multiplier.
He would further submit that the deceased received injuries on 21.9.1992 and is survived upto 22.10.1996.
So, precisely, the multiplier of 4 could be attributed while assessing the just and fair compensation.
He would further submit that even it is not believed by the learned Tribunal that the deceased died due to the injury he received from the road accident.

He would further submit that the findings arrived at by the learned Tribunal that there is no nexus between the injuries and death of the deceased is not challenged by the claimant by filing cross objection or cross appeal.

He would further submit that since after receiving injury,
the deceased survived for only four years, multiplier of 4 could be applied by considering that he has suffered 100% permanent disabilities.
He would further submit that therefore, the learned Tribunal has committed serious error in adopting multiplier 12 instead of 4.
Upon such submission, he prays to modify the impugned judgment and award.
4. Per contra, learned advocate for respondents - original claimants would submit that since the learned Tribunal has not calculated the future prospective, the same may be calculated.
However, he would fairly submit that multiplier of 4 could be adopted.

He would further submit that compensation under the head of loss of estate and loss of consortium may be enhanced so also compensation under the head of future NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4555/2008 ORDER DATED:
08/10/2024 undefined expenses.
Upon such submission, he prays to modify the judgment and award suitably.
5. Apt to note that the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is a beneficial piece of Legislation.
The concept of just and fair compensation is integral and seminal to the MV Act.

The compensation to be awarded under the principle of just and fair compensation to the injured of the road accident or the legal representative/s of the deceased person is based on the principle of fairness, reasonableness and equability.

Anguish of the heart or for mental turbulence being consequential result of the road accident cannot be actually compensated, but the quint essentiality lies in adopting holistic and pragmatic view to the computation of the compensation for the loss sustained, which is to be in the realm of realistic approximation.
Although exact or perfect arithmetical calculation of compensation for reparation of the loss arrived from the road accident is almost impossible.
The Tribunal is bestowed with duty to make an endevour to award just compensation regardless of the amount claimed by the claimant.
The determination of the quantum of compensation therefore, must be liberal and not niggardly since the law values life and limb in a free country in generous scale.

Needless to state that money may be awarded, so that something tangible may be procured to reach something else of the like nature, which has been destroyed or lost, but money cannot renew physical frame that has been battered and shattered being a result of the road accident.

Yet Tribunal to endavour to bring back victim to stage of pre-road accident as far as possible Thus, the award must be reasonable and cannot be assessed NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4555/2008 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined with moderation though it cannot at the same time be pity and what could be granted must be just, fair and equitable compensation.

sentences.text: I have considered the submissions made by the rival parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings of the Tribunal.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the learned Tribunal.

From the record, it transpires that the learned Tribunal has taken up the income of the deceased of Rs.4500/- per month, which is substantiated by the evidence on record, but did not grant prospective income, deducted 1/3rd towards the personal expenses and calculated dependency loss of Rs.36000/- per month applying multiplier of 12 to arrive at loss of dependency at Rs.4,32,000/- and granted compensation under the head of loss of estate, loss of consortium,
funeral expenses, transport expenses and thus, granted total compensation Rs.4,72,000/-.
6.2
Noticeably, the learned Tribunal adopted multiplier of 12 taking up the age of the deceased at the time of road accident.
Notably, the learned Tribunal failed to notice that the deceased after receiving several injuries on 21.9.1992 had survived upto 22.10.1996.
The learned Tribunal in categorical finding held that the claimant has failed to establish the nexus or link between the injuries received by him and the death.
Thus, it is established that the deceased did not die due to the injury he has received from the road accident.

The deceased therefore, survived for four years after receiving the injuries from the road accident and therefore, multiplier of 4 should be applied and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4555/2008 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined hence, the learned Tribunal has committed serious error in applying multiplier of 12 instead of 4.
6.3

Therefore, total compensation would be as under, which the claimant/s is/are entitled to get.
 Particulars Amo  Actual income 45  Prospective income (30%)
Future dependency Loss 2  Loss of Estate   Loss of consortium   Funeral expenses   Transportation expenses   medical expenses
Total...
Less : Amount which is already awarded 4  Refund amount to be awarded to the 1  insurance company 7.
Therefore, I hold that the insurance company is entitled to refund back the amount of Rs.1,96,676/- with accrued interest, which would meet the ends of justice.
Rest of the direction(s) of the Tribunal remain same.
8. For the reasons recorded above, the following order is passed.
8.1 The present appeal is partly allowed.

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4555/2008 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined 8.2
The claimants are entitled to have compensation of Rs.2,75,324/- along with 8.5% interest per annum from the date of filing the claim petition till realization.

8.3 Since the insurance company has deposited entire decretal amount of Rs.4,72,000/- along with accrued interest thereon, after deducting just and fair compensation of Rs.2,75,324/- along with accrued interest thereon.
The learned Tribunal is directed to refund the amount Rs.1,96,676/- with accrued interest to the appellant - insurance company forthwith.
8.4 If any amount is paid excess than the amount of Rs.2,75,324/- to the claimant, it shall not be recovered from the claimant.
8.5 While making the payment, the Tribunal shall deduct the courts fees, if not paid, in accordance with rules/law.
8.6 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
